name: Greece

nso.name: Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT, Elliniki Statistiki Archi)

latest_census.notes: The Population-Housing Census 2021 (and 2011, 2001) records citizenship and country of birth only. Religion and mother tongue were last asked in the 1951 census and have been omitted since; Greece has never asked an ethnicity item. The Muslim minority of Thrace and the packet's national religion range are estimates, not census counts.

subnational_sources.title: Census 2021 / 2011: resident population by citizenship (Greek, EU, non-EU, by country of citizenship), by region and regional unit
subnational_sources.evidence: Listed only to record that the one subnational identity table Greece publishes is citizenship, which is nationality, not ethnicity, and is not a substitute for any of the three fields.

tier_reason: The Greek census has not asked religion or language since 1951 and has never asked ethnicity; there is no count to find at any geography.
recommended_action: Declare religion, ethnicity and language not_collected for Greece and propagate to the 8 admin1 and 14 admin2 shapes, citing 'last asked in the 1951 census; the 2001, 2011 and 2021 censuses record citizenship and country of birth only'. Eurostat is already handled by the adapter. Do not substitute citizenship for ethnicity.
not_found: Any post-1951 official count of religion or mother tongue in Greece
summary: Greece is a clean Tier C: the 2021 census, like 2011 and 2001, asks citizenship and country of birth and nothing on religion, ethnicity or language; religion and mother tongue were last asked in 1951. All three fields should be declared not_collected at national, admin1 (8) and admin2 (14) level. ELSTAT's citizenship-by-regional-unit tables exist but are nationality, not ethnicity, and should not be used as a stand-in.
